title: FlashAttention with Statistics: Low-Overhead Attention Features for Compact Hallucination Detectors
authors: Volodichev, Savichev, Sviridov, Yuliy, Simakov, Zaytsev (Applied AI Institute / Yandex / Risk AI Research Lab)

setup.source: arXiv:2610.21483v1 (Volodichev, Savichev, Sviridov, Yuliy, Simakov, Zaytsev; Applied AI Institute / Yandex / Risk AI Research Lab, 15 Oct 2026, 28 pp)
setup.method: FlashAttention with Statistics: per-head attention statistics computed inside the FA2 forward, ordered into four tiers by the extra work they cost, feeding compact hallucination detectors
setup.setting: one head of one layer; prompt of P tokens then R = L-P response tokens, teacher-forced in ONE call; prompt rows go to any production kernel; the response stage evaluates Q_R against all K,V with the causal mask aligned to the BOTTOM-RIGHT corner
setup.response_block_scores: N_R = R*P + R(R+1)/2 unmasked scores per head
setup.online_softmax: FA2 forward is QUERY-MAJOR; carries (m, ell, O); o = O/ell and LSE = m + log ell after the last tile; FA stores the LSE so a later kernel recovers any weight

tiers.T1_fused: no extra scores; O(N_s*N_R) statistic ops; N_s*R numbers written; entropy, prompt mass, effective support, max weight
tiers.T2_lookup: bR extra scores from the STORED LSE; log p_ii, p_{i,i-1}, fixed-sink weight; works after ANY kernel that stores LSE
tiers.T3_rescore: N_R extra scores; key-major loop of the FA2 BACKWARD with dO replaced by a column of ones; column sums and sink rates; one key tile per instance, NO atomic additions
tiers.T4_dense: N_R extra scores and Omega(N_R) memory; MTopDiv, stored maps, row top-k mass; the authors wrote NO T4 kernel

setup.lemma1: F_i = sum_j p_ij^alpha_u g_u(i,j,s_ij) with integer alpha_u >= 1 and fixed-dimensional g_u independent of m/ell/LSE is computable in the pass with no extra exponentials or scores, using sum_u dim(g_u) state per row INDEPENDENT of L
setup.eq3_eq4: A_u = sum_seen e^{alpha(s_j-m)} g_u; A_u <- a^alpha A_u + rowsum(Pt^alpha * G_u); finalize A_u/ell^alpha

instances.entropy: H = LSE - F, alpha=1, g=s UNSHIFTED
instances.max_weight: 1/ell, needs m to be the EXACT running maximum

setup.appC_merge: A_u = e^{alpha(m1-m)}A_{u,1} + e^{alpha(m2-m)}A_{u,2}, m = max(m1,m2); ASSOCIATIVE, so keys may split across kernel instances or devices; factors in (0,1], 1 <= ell <= |J_i|

feature_blocks.A7: K strongest induction heads, 22 candidates; App L.1's seven kept: max weight (mean,std,max), effective support (min), normalized entropy (mean,std), BOS sink rate
feature_blocks.A64: every head of every layer, k largest cbar_j from T3, concatenated, standardized, 64 PCs; no selection
feature_blocks.H64: ONE middle layer without selection (14 for 0.6B/1.7B, 18 for 4B/8B, 1-based), mean + population std over answer tokens, standardized, 64 randomized PCs, standardized again
feature_blocks.L9: nine of 224 candidates from seven per-token next-token-distribution statistics x four pools, kept by recursive feature elimination

setup.probe: class-balanced L2 logistic regression (liblinear), C in {0.001,0.01,0.1,1,10} by validation AUROC, threshold by validation F1; models NOT refit on train+val; K in {1,2,4,8,16,32}, k in 1..10 by grouped five-fold CV
setup.statistics: 100,000 paired bootstrap resamples of TEST GROUPS (seed 42); p = (1 + #{|delta*_b - delta| >= |delta|})/(B+1); Holm over the 12 dataset-proxy pairs of each addition
setup.kernel_support: GQA, bf16/fp16/fp8-e5m2, head dims 64/128/256, key keep mask; statistic families are compile-time flags; NO sliding-window and NO soft-capped attention
setup.hardware: single NVIDIA H100 NVL, bf16; Triton for T1-T3, eager PyTorch for T4
setup.toy_spec: local probes use CPU float32/float64 tensors (L<=1024, d=32, 4 heads); no Triton, no H100, no Qwen3 backbone, no RAGTruth/HaluBench/TRIVIA+ harness. Tier WORK COUNTS and BYTES are measured; Table 5's milliseconds are anchors only

evidence: the paper gives an anonymous.4open.science repository (attention-guardrails-0C16) rather than a named author GitHub account, consistent with double-blind review
the kernels are described as Triton for T1-T3 and eager PyTorch for T4, with a HuggingFace attention backend installed only on the scored layers
App D gives Algorithm 1 verbatim (28 lines, black = unchanged FA2 forward, green = additions tagged by tier), so the mechanism is reproducible from the paper alone
the authors state they wrote NO T4 kernel
repo_audit.reproduction_basis: PDF text layer (28 pp): main text Sec 1-6 + Appendices A-M. All tables and figure coordinates in this module are transcribed from that text layer; every local probe is a declared synthetic stand-in
recorded_observations: Sec 5.2's prose enumeration of A7 lists 18 items while the block is named A7 and App L.1's seven kept features are authoritative; the 22-candidate count needs FIVE per-token statistics while the prose names four, so the fifth (prompt mass) is a DECLARED resolution, not a published one
App B states that restricting LLM-Check and SinkProbe to response rows IS A DIFFERENT FEATURE from the published all-token versions and that the two versions were not compared in detection
the paper NAMES INTRYGUE's entropy gate and TOHA's MTopDiv but gives NEITHER formula
Table 14's Mean column EXCLUDES the fitting domain for fit-on-one rows and covers all six for the other-five/all-six rows (verified locally)
row top-k mass needs O(k) state per row, so Lemma 1 does not cover it and it belongs to T4 - 'T1 does not contain every bounded-state reduction'
Qwen3 defines no BOS token; the authors call its first non-padded token BOS, and T2 obtains the BOS sink rate without full column sums only when every sequence in the batch has the same padding
limitations_recorded: tiers are not claimed exhaustive and bound cost from ABOVE; a T4 statistic may admit an efficient kernel the authors did not write; no optimality claim
the response kernel is faster than FA2 on Hopper but SLOWER than cuDNN

NOT a production kernel: statistics are for a complete response in one call; token-by-token generation needs a split-KV decoding kernel, possible because T1 accumulators merge associatively but NOT implemented
no sliding-window and no soft-capped attention; padding mask only; head dims 64/128/256
the wrapper copies both stage outputs into one tensor (avoidable via a separate prefill)

the proxy needs an auxiliary forward and labeled probe-training examples; a small proxy may miss evidence; support is RELATIVE TO SUPPLIED CONTEXT, not general factual truth; scores need separate calibration
end-to-end results only reach 8.4K; long-context end-to-end is future work
repo_audit.ethical_considerations: the paper aims to make detection cheap enough to check every RAG response, but it can miss unsupported answers or flag supported ones, so in high-stakes settings it should COMPLEMENT HUMAN REVIEW, NOT REPLACE IT. Public benchmarks under their terms; no new data, no human subjects.
no_claims: no claim of reproducing the H100 NVL Triton latencies or peak-memory figures
no claim of reproducing RAGTruth QA / HaluBench / TRIVIA+ detection scores
no claim of running any Qwen3 proxy or any of the nine LLM judges
no claim that the local synthetic probes reproduce Table 4's real-input MAEs (random Gaussian inputs hide sinks and peaked heads)
no claim that the INTRYGUE gate or TOHA MTopDiv stand-ins are the published formulas, which the paper does not give

table1_tiers_data.tier_ordering: tiers are ordered by EXTRA SCORES; a tier is the path the authors' implementation uses and bounds cost from ABOVE. The LSE belongs to no tier.
table1_tiers_data.declared_adaptation: Table 1's entries are pure arithmetic in (R, L, N_R). The closed form is verified by MATERIALIZING the response block at L up to 4096; the L=32768 row is computed analytically because the visibility matrix alone would need ~2.5 GiB on this host. No kernel timing is claimed anywhere.

algorithm1_data.declared_adaptation: score counters are TILE-GRANULAR: a diagonal-crossing tile evaluates its masked entries too, so the count is a superset of the ideal N_R (ratio -> 1 as tile_k -> 1). Recorded, never asserted equal.

bounds.note: App C: m' >= m and m' >= s_j, so a = exp(m-m') and every merge factor lie in (0,1]; the maximizing key contributes one, giving 1 <= ell <= |J_i|

appc_merge_data.why_it_matters: associativity is what permits keys split across kernel instances or devices (RingAttention, Attention-as-RNN, FlashInfer), and what would make a split-KV DECODING kernel possible - the paper did not implement one.
appc_merge_data.tolerance_note: the merge formula is algebraically exact, but the pass runs in fp32 and a split changes the ACCUMULATION ORDER, so the comparison is made at fp32 precision: relative diff < 1e-5 against max(1, |statistic|). eff_support = ell^2/A_2 is a reciprocal of a small sum and reaches ~2e2 here, so its absolute diff (~1e-4) is ~5e-7 relative. Both the absolute and relative worst cases are reported, never hidden.

local_probe.input_type: random Gaussian Q,K,V (paper Q1 synthetic arm)

table4_accuracy_data.declared_adaptation: the local arm uses random Gaussian Q,K,V, which give near-uniform attention and HIDE sinks and peaked heads, so its ratios exceed the paper's 1e3-1e4. It reports DIRECTION, not magnitude. The paper's real inputs come from Qwen3-8B layers 2/16/24/34.
table4_accuracy_data.negative_result_recorded: the dense bf16 arm must round the SCORES and recompute LSE and the weights in the rounded dtype; passing the fp64 LSE through unrounded gives the baseline a free exact normalizer and forces its LSE MAE to 0.0.

published_ranges.note: Latency overhead % of ONE attention layer, L in {16K,32K}; columns d=64/128/256 at r=0.1/0.3/0.5. <=T2 adds at most 5 percentage points over <=T1; both add 1-30% over Base; <=T3 is costliest at 16-87%. 4K excluded (fixed host time).

table5_latency_data.finding: T1 and T2 are cheap enough to compute together BY DEFAULT; T3 is worthwhile only when a detector needs reductions over all final weights.
table5_latency_data.declared_adaptation: no H100 and no Triton on this host, so every percentage is a published anchor. The local contribution is the RECOMPUTED ordering and the <=5pp gap, plus the work counts in paper_fas_table1_tiers. On the response stage alone <=T3 takes 1.7-1.8x Base at d>=128 and 2.1-2.2x at d=64 - the arithmetic of a second QK^T pass, not register pressure.

paper_claims.Q7: 4B proxy beats the best of nine judges on HaluBench and TRIVIA+; 0.6B on RAGTruth QA; A64H64 beats prompting the SAME backbone in all 12 pairs

table2_f1_data.declared_adaptation: the grid is transcribed exactly; no Qwen3 proxy is run here. The local contribution is recomputing Q4/Q5/Q7 from the cells rather than restating them.

table10_auroc_data.note: A64 beats A7 alone in all 12 pairs in BOTH F1 and AUROC; the best judge still leads on AUROC (.909/.859/.786) while A64H64 beats prompting the SAME backbone everywhere.
table10_auroc_data.declared_adaptation: transcribed cells; no proxy is run here.

checks.significance_rule: significant iff delta > 0 AND Holm p < 0.05

tables11_12_additions_data.paper_abstract: attention features significantly improve F1 in 6 of 12 benchmark x proxy pairs and never significantly lower it
tables11_12_additions_data.declared_adaptation: p-values are the published Holm-corrected cells (p < .001 encoded as .0005, strictly below the threshold); the bootstrap itself is not re-run at 100,000 resamples here. The local contribution is recomputing WHICH pairs are significant and checking the abstract's 6-of-12 count.

appk_length_data.declared_adaptation: the local demo is a synthetic length-biased world, not HaluEval. It exists to show WHY a tie-aware AUROC is required: after the filter every (length, label) cell holds the same count, so the length score carries no label information and the correct value is exactly 0.5. A ranks-by-argsort implementation that does not average ties returns an arbitrary extreme instead.
appk_length_data.paper_warning: App B states that restricting LLM-Check and SinkProbe to response rows IS A DIFFERENT FEATURE from the published all-token versions, and the two were not compared in detection.

appm_transfer_data.declared_adaptation: Table 14 is transcribed; the local contribution is verifying that the published Mean column EXCLUDES the fitting domain for fit-on-one rows (INTRYGUE fit RAGTruth: mean of .77 .55 .48 .41 .92 = .62) and covers all six for the other-five/all-six rows. Intervals use 1,000 resamples of INDIVIDUAL TEST EXAMPLES, not groups.
appm_transfer_data.paper_gap: the paper NAMES INTRYGUE's gate and TOHA's MTopDiv but gives NEITHER formula; both are declared adaptations wherever they are implemented locally.

cost_memory_data.finding: the wrapper adds a FIXED 47-60 ms host cost per forward while GPU work grows only 5 ms on short 8B inputs; per scored layer it launches 88 more kernels and reads ten values back. CUDA graphs could remove most of it. Extra peak grows with RESPONSE tokens, not with the prompt.
cost_memory_data.declared_adaptation: every millisecond, MiB and kernel count is a published anchor measured on an H100 NVL with Qwen3-8B/0.6B. No such hardware or backbone is available here; the local contribution is the recomputed deltas and orderings.
